key_insight: A pulse-and-coupling modulation protocol enables high-fidelity two-qubit gates and state transfer even when quantum emitters have significant spectral mismatch or noise.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical route to scalable solid-state quantum interconnects that can exceed the fault-tolerance threshold despite emitter-to-emitter detuning.
method: Drive qubits with pulses at the cavity frequency for low-damping cavities.
Periodically modulate qubit–cavity coupling to compensate spectral differences.
For high damping, operate in the dispersive regime with far-detuned pulses.
evidence_signal: Analytical and numerical results show that, with modest inter-pulse delay, fidelity can rise from strongly suppressed levels to above 99.9% for two-qubit state transfer.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful timing, cavity damping regime, and control of pulse/coupling modulation, which may be challenging in hardware.
paper_title: Scalable Photon-Mediated Two-Qubit Gates with Spectrally Noisy Quantum Emitters
